items.title: Offering Zero Data Retention for frontier models
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirms its commitment to Zero Data Retention for eligible API customers, ensuring that no data is stored after processing. Additionally, the company introduces Private Safety Processing, a feature aimed at enhancing AI safety without compromising user data privacy. This move highlights OpenAI's focus on user privacy and security, especially for advanced AI models.
items.why_it_matters: This enhances data privacy protocols for developers using frontier models, crucial for building trust with end-users.

items.title: Domain and publish date filters for Web Search on AgentCore
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's Web Search now supports runtime domain and publish-date filtering, allowing developers to control source freshness and relevance in real-time. These filters are enforced server-side, providing a robust mechanism for precise data retrieval. This update also includes an expansion of Web Search capabilities within the platform.
items.why_it_matters: Improves control over data sourcing, essential for developing applications that rely on up-to-date and relevant information.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments is now generally available
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments are now generally available, enabling AI agents to autonomously conduct transactions at scale. The service includes built-in spending guardrails and protocol-agnostic payment orchestration, ensuring secure operations with comprehensive observability.

items.title: Replit expands access with GPT-5.6 Luna
items.summary: Replit introduces a Free Mode powered by GPT-5.6 Luna, allowing users to create software without incurring token costs. This makes software development more accessible and removes financial barriers for users looking to transform ideas into functional applications.

items.title: Position: Collusion Risks Among AI Reasoning Agents Justify Certification Requirements
items.summary: A position paper argues that AI agents with chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities may exhibit collusive behavior. The paper suggests that such agents should obtain behavioral certification before making market-related decisions to ensure ethical and unbiased operations.

This release also expands Web Search to the Europe (Ireland) and Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Regions.
